edition.locus: Gebhardt III.II (Rusticus questions Justin; the creed)

source_text: Ὡς εἰσαχθέντων πρὸ τοῦ βήματος Ῥουστικὸς ὁ ἔπαρχος εἶπε πρὸς Ἰουστῖνον· Πρῶτον πείσθητι τοῖς θεοῖς καὶ ὑπάκουσον τοῖς βασιλεῦσιν. Ἰουστῖνος εἶπεν· Ἄμεμπτον καὶ ἀκατάγνωστον τὸ πείθεσθαι τοῖς προσταχθεῖσιν ὑπὸ τοῦ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ. Ῥουστικὸς ἔπαρχος εἶπεν· Ποίους λόγους μεταχειρίζῃ; Ἰουστῖνος εἶπεν· Πάντας μὲν λόγους ἐπειράθην μαθεῖν, συνεθέμην δὲ τοῖς ἀληθέσι λόγοις τοῖς τῶν Χριστιανῶν, κἂν μὴ ἀρέσκωσι τοῖς ψευδοδόξοις. Ῥουστικὸς ἔπαρχος εἶπεν· Ἐκεῖνοί σε ἀρέσκουσιν οἱ λόγοι, πανάθλιε; Ἰουστῖνος εἶπεν· Ναί, ἐπειδὴ μετὰ δόγματος ὀρθοῦ ἕπομαι αὐτοῖς. Ῥουστικὸς ἔπαρχος εἶπεν· Ποῖόν ἐστι δόγμα; Ἰουστῖνος εἶπεν· Ὃ εὐσεβοῦμεν εἰς τὸν τῶν Χριστιανῶν θεόν, ὃν ἡγούμεθα ἕνα τοῦτον ἐξ ἀρχῆς ποιητὴν καὶ δημιουργὸν τῆς πάσης κτίσεως, ὁρατῆς τε καὶ ἀοράτου, καὶ κύριον Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν παῖδα θεοῦ, ὃς καὶ προκεκήρυκται ὑπὸ τῶν προφητῶν μέλλων παραγίνεσθαι τῷ γένει τῶν ἀνθρώπων σωτηρίας κήρυξ καὶ διδάσκαλος καλῶν μαθημάτων. Κἀγὼ ἄνθρωπος ὢν μικρὰ νομίζω λέγειν πρὸς τὴν αὐτοῦ ἄπειρον θεότητα, προφητικὴν τινά δύναμιν ὁμολογῶν· ἐπεὶ προκεκήρυκται περὶ τούτου ὃν ἔφην νῦν θεοῦ υἱὸν ὄντα· ἃ γὰρ ἄνωθεν προεῖπον οἱ προφῆται περὶ τῆς τούτου παρουσίας γενομένης ἐν ἀνθρώποις.
pass_a_gloss: With them having been led in before the tribunal, Rusticus the prefect said to Justin: first yield to the gods and hearken to the emperors. Justin said: without blame and without condemnation is the yielding to the things enjoined by our savior Jesus Christ. The prefect Rusticus said: what teachings do you handle. Justin said: every teaching I tried to learn, but I agreed with the true teachings, the ones of the Christians, even if they do not please the falsely-opining. The prefect Rusticus said: those teachings — do they please you, most-miserable one. Justin said: yes, since with right tenet I follow them. The prefect Rusticus said: what sort is the tenet. Justin said: which we worship toward the god of the Christians, whom we hold this one from beginning maker and fashioner of the whole creation, both seen and unseen, and lord Jesus Christ servant of god, who also was heralded-before by the prophets as about to be present to the race of men as proclaimer of salvation and teacher of fine learnings. And I, man being, deem it trifling to speak toward his boundless godhead, acknowledging some prophetic power; since it was heralded-before about this one whom I just called being son of god; for what from above the prophets said-before about his advent that happened among men.
pass_b_english: When they had been brought before the tribunal, Rusticus the prefect said to Justin, “First yield to the gods and obey the emperors.” Justin said, “It is blameless and beyond condemnation to obey what was commanded by our Savior Jesus Christ.” Rusticus the prefect said, “What teachings do you profess?” Justin said, “I tried to learn every teaching, but I gave my assent to the true teachings, those of the Christians, even if they do not please men of false opinion.” Rusticus the prefect said, “Do those teachings please you, you utter wretch?” Justin said, “Yes, since I follow them with right doctrine.”.

Rusticus the prefect said, “What sort of doctrine is it?” Justin said, “That in which we worship the God of the Christians, whom we hold to be the one Maker from the beginning and Fashioner of the whole creation, seen and unseen, and the Lord Jesus Christ, servant of God, who was also foretold by the prophets as about to come to the race of men as a herald of salvation and a teacher of good lessons. And I, being a man, count it a small thing to speak concerning his boundless Godhead, acknowledging a certain prophetic power, since beforehand proclamation was made concerning him whom I just now said is Son of God, namely the things the prophets of old foretold concerning his advent which took place among men.”.

lemmas.gloss: raised tribunal platform before which trial happens
yield, be persuaded, obey here as compliance order
child or servant, here of Christ to God

choices.why: aorist passive imperative of peitho with dative, a command to comply rather than inner belief, matching the prefect's demand for obedience
pais in trial-confession context paired with kyrios points to servant role, while the same passage immediately after uses huios for sonship distinctly
meta with genitive gives accompaniment, and dogma here means the tenet followed, not merely an act of opinion

variants: μαθημάτων M (adopted) against μαθητῶν codd.: 'teacher of fine teachings', not 'of pupils'.
